content.title: About
content.content: Canned quail eggs are whole quail eggs that have been heat‑treated and sealed in an airtight jar. Quail eggs are small (about 1 cm in diameter) and have a richer flavor, higher nutrient density, and a long shelf life compared with chicken eggs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Quail eggs contain roughly 2‑3 times more protein, vitamin B12, and iron than chicken eggs.
In Japan, canned quail eggs are often served in soy sauce as a snack with sake.
Traditional Chinese medicine uses quail eggs to boost immunity and improve eyesight.
A sealed jar of quail eggs can be stored at room temperature for 2‑3 years if unopened.
In the 1950s, canning quail eggs became popular in the USSR as a way to extend food supplies during shortages.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Quail eggs provide about 13 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: High in vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Source of iron and selenium
items.content: These minerals act as antioxidants and help maintain a strong immune system.

items.title: Low cholesterol
items.content: Quail eggs contain less cholesterol than chicken eggs, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains vitamins A and D
items.content: Vitamins A and D support vision, skin health, and bone metabolism.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: People allergic to eggs may experience reactions ranging from hives to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned eggs are often salted; individuals with hypertension should monitor their intake.

items.title: Bacterial risk if seal is broken
items.content: A bulging or leaking jar may indicate contamination with Clostridium botulinum.

items.title: Not for infants under 1 year
items.content: Due to allergy risk and digestibility, whole quail eggs are not recommended for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned quail eggs can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, soups, rice dishes, or served as a snack with alcohol. They are also sliced for sandwiches or included in bento boxes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, refrigerate and consume within 5‑7 days.
